sense: of grapes or berries; a cluster

evidence: Verg. G. 2.60: fert ūva racēmōs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Properly the stalk of a cluster, then the cluster itself; it hangs as grapes, dates and the like do (Plin. NH 15.115). Mattioli has racēmātim, “in clusters” (M-O).

terms.gloss: a bunch of grapes; a grape
terms.comment: The grape (see grape), and by extension a whole bunch, as Traupman gives it. Collectively, grapes.

terms.register: vōx plērumque poētica: Verg., Ov., Prop.
terms.comment: A cluster of berries or flowers, above all of ivy; mostly in verse.

phrases.latin: tempus ut extēnsīs tumeat facit ūva racēmīs
phrases.english: time makes the grape swell on its stretched clusters

sources: Lewis & Short: racemus · Lewis & Short: uva · Lewis & Short: corymbus
Ovid from the Latinitas loci collection (loci-ovidius); the other passages as Lewis & Short quotes them.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 323.
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. cluster.
